title: Bobby Boyd: OU Quarterback Turned Colts Interceptions Leader
question: Which former Oklahoma quarterback became a star defensive back for the Baltimore Colts?
answer: Bobby Boyd (OU 1957-59) moved from quarterback to cornerback in the pros and intercepted 57 passes for the Baltimore Colts from 1960 to 1968. He then coached on the Colts staff and opened a Baltimore-area restaurant.
summary: Bobby Boyd played for Bud Wilkinson at OU from 1957 to 1959, then picked off 57 passes for the Colts, joined their staff and opened a Towson restaurant.
body: Bobby Boyd (OU 1957-59) played for Bud Wilkinson at Oklahoma, starting out as a halfback before shifting to quarterback ahead of the 1958 season while still playing defense. He earned first-team All-Big Eight recognition in 1959.

Baltimore took him in the 10th round of the 1960 NFL Draft, and the Colts decided his future was in the secondary. Boyd spent all nine of his pro seasons in Baltimore, from 1960 through 1968, and finished with 57 interceptions. That total tied him for 13th in NFL history when he retired and stands second in Colts history behind Ed Reed.

He made two Pro Bowls and was part of the Colts team that won the 1968 NFL championship. After retiring as a player in 1969 he stayed with the club as a coach, and he was on the staff when Baltimore won Super Bowl V in January 1971.

Away from the sideline, Boyd opened a bar and restaurant in Towson, Maryland, called Bobby Boyd's Hooligans, and he later worked in the restaurant business with Colts great Johnny Unitas. In 1986 he moved back to Garland, Texas.
Boyd died in August 2017 at age 79. For Sooner fans, he is a reminder that Wilkinson's quarterbacks could do more than run the offense.
